territorial_scope.description: Applies to Department of Defense contracting under United States federal law.

evidence.quote: The Secretary of Defense shall, in contracting provisions with cloud providers, foundation model providers, and data infrastructure providers

summary.short: If enacted, requires the Secretary of Defense to use competitive awards, retain government data rights and prioritize multi-cloud technology in contracts with cloud, data infrastructure and foundation model providers, and to bar training commercial AI products on Defense data without authorization.
summary.long: The bill would direct the Secretary of Defense, in contracts with cloud, data infrastructure and foundation model providers, to require a competitive award for each procurement of cloud computing, data infrastructure or foundation model solutions, to keep exclusive Government rights to Government data, and to prioritize multi-cloud technology unless infeasible or a substantial danger to national security. It defines covered providers as those with Department of Defense contracts totaling at least $50,000,000 in the five previous fiscal years. It directs the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office to update the DFARS so that Government-furnished data for AI development is not used to train or improve commercial products of covered providers without express Department authorization, and it provides that violations are subject to specific penalties, including fines and contract termination. Component acquisition executives may grant exemptions for national security, with notice to the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer. The Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff must report annually for four years, beginning by January 15, 2027, on AI competition and market concentration, listing exemptions granted, and the report must be publicly posted on a Department of Defense website.

Text points: (1) Sec. 2(c) names the 'Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office' while Sec. 2(c)(4)(B) names the 'Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer'. (2) Sec. 2(d)(1) 'annually thereafter for four years' is ambiguous (four reports in total or four after the first). (3) 'Department of Defense data decrees' and 'Creating Data Advantage (Open DAGIR) principles' are used without definition or citation.
